text:
liz: FYI — customer reports intermittent 429s and big tail latency on their Dedicated pool (eu1-reserved). Started ~48h ago, p95/p99 spikes coincide with auth 429s. They see short bursts only on a subset of nodes. Can ops grab initial triage?

rahul: on it. any node ids or sample request ids from the customer?

liz: provided node ids: node-az1-132, node-az1-139. sample request id 2026-06-14T08:03:21Z req=acme-req-7f3. Customer logs show: 
```
2026-06-14T08:03:21Z ERROR auth: 429 slice-throttle tenant=acme pool=eu1-reserved slice=1
2026-06-14T08:03:21Z WARN runtime: tail-latency spike p99=2.3s p95=1.1s
```

andrea: quick glance at telemetry for node-az1-132: MIG slice 1 SM util ~88-95% during spikes, sibling slices <10%. NVLink and DRAM BW look healthy. suggests noisy neighbor within same GPU package (MIG partition).

mike: can you confirm autoscaler events? if mins dropped and we got packed fractional slices that could make one slice hit SM hot.

rahul: checked autoscaler logs — there were small scale-downs overnight: pool eu1-reserved scaled from 4->3 around 02:12 UTC, then back 3->4 at 02:22. There are a bunch of short-lived eviction/repack events.

liz: repro steps from customer (they ran this against model-x-13b):
1) send 40 concurrent streaming requests of ~1k tokens
2) after 30s, observe 5-10% of requests returning 429s and p99s spike
They included curl snippet: 
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED"  -H "x-tenant: acme"  -d '{"model":"model-x-13b","input":"<long prompt>"}'  https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate --parallel 40
```

andrea: hypothesis: fractional MIG packing + transient autoscale causes one slice to get hot (continuous batching on that slice). KV-cache locality could be amplifying. two mitigations: 1) pin tenant to dedicated slice (isolate) or 2) increase pool min to avoid scale-down churn.

mike: temporary mitigation steps I recommend now:
- set pool eu1-reserved.autoscale.min to 4 for 2h
- pin tenant acme to slice-affinity=exclusive (ops command below)

Command: 
```
infractl pool update eu1-reserved --autoscale-min 4
infractl tenant set-affinity acme --exclusive-slice node-az1-132:1
```

rahul: running `nvidia-smi dmon -s u` on node-az1-132 now, will paste samples in a minute.

sre-bot: ALERT node-az1-132: MIG-slice-1 SM=92% mem=45% p99-latency=2130ms (detected 3 spikes in last 10m)

rahul: paste of dmon snapshot: 
```
# gpu   sm   mem   enc   dec
0     92    45    1     0
0     90    44    0     0
```

andrea: that's pretty convincing. also check kernel preemption counts and context-switches on that slice, and whether continuous-batching is pushing the KV-cache misses.

liz: I'm going to reach out to customer with temporary mitigation and ask them to re-run load after we bump min and pin. I'll schedule an on-call window for 1hr.

mike: long-term: eng-runtime should consider soft-affinity policy so autoscaler avoids repacking slices with active KV-locality. tagging @andrea for a small RFC. :thinking_face:

andrea: noted. I'll draft a short RFC with data from these nodes. Also recommend adding a throttle reason tag in telemetry when slice SM>85% to make this pattern searchable.

rahul: applied autoscale.min=4 and set affinity to exclusive for acme. monitoring.

liz: thanks — customer notified, they will test in 15m and update. will escalate to eng-runtime if we see >2 recurrences after mitigation. :thumbsup:

mike: ack. assigning follow-up to @rahul and @andrea.

sre-bot: NOTE created incident INC-2026-3325 assigned to infra oncall

liz: closing loop here once customer confirms, will attach logs and the dmon snippet to INC-2026-3325.

rahul: quick note — found small kernel OOM kill in pod logs for a helper container, unrelated but cleaned up.

andrea: cool. if customer still sees 429s after isolation we'll repro locally with a 40x 1k token streaming harness against model-x-13b and open a runtime regression.

liz: thanks team.
